newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Chan plans to keep job, denies threat to quit.
newsitem.headline: HK's Chan plans to keep job, denies threat to quit.

text.p: Hong Kong's top civil servant Anson Chan plans to stay in her job after the territory reverts to China and denied she had any intentions of leaving before retirement in three years.

The highly-popular Chief Secretary and deputy to British governor Chris Patten, made her comments during an interview with cable news network CNN, backtracking on earlier hints that she might quit if asked to accept policies that clashed with her principles..
"I don't really envisage leaving my post before my normal retirement age," Chan, 57, told CNN.
"I did not, and I repeat, I did not threaten to resign."
Her remarks follow weeks of intense speculation that there might be a growing rift between her and her future boss, Tung Chee-hwa, after Britain hands Hong Kong back to China on July 1.

Chan, who accepted an offer from Tung last year to stay on in her post after the handover, told Newsweek magazine last month that while she was a loyal civil servant, loyalty was not everything in her eyes.
"There might be issues that are points of principle and as a matter of conscience, you feel you can't accept those decisions," she had told Newsweek.
"When that happens, you start asking yourself 'Do I stay or do I go?' And I think most people would know what my answer would be," she was quoted as saying.
